notes:
Summary: Summit Telemetry is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency routing of telemetry triage and a real-time support chat overlay. They want hard guarantees for throughput and predictable reserved pricing. Key constraints: VPC-only control plane, SOC2 + SSO, and EU data residency for part of their fleet.

Throughput & latency targets: aiming for 1.5k concurrent chat sessions with 95th percentile latency < 120ms for short-chat responses (prompt+generation), and reranking pipeline must handle 5k qps at 512 token context with <70ms p95 for rerank inference. They provided sample traffic histograms (drive link).

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask = capacity equivalent to 8x A100-80GB (baseline) with ability to burst + 2x spare across a second region. Want cost predictability for committed monthly capacity and clear overage pricing. They're open to a hybrid: Dedicated for primary region + private for EU residency.

SLA negotiation points: uptime >= 99.95% for dedicated clusters, credits scale for sustained downtime; explicit SLO for p95 latency (target above) with penalties or extra capacity credits. Also want guaranteed model compatibility matrix for fallback variants and a guarantee that cross-region failover won't increase token egress unexpectedly. Finance is pushing for a cap on unexpected egress.

Reliability & fallback design discussed:
- Cross-region failover: prefer active-passive with automated DNS + health checks; warm standby in secondary region with pre-warmed KV caches. Discussed acceptable RTO ~30s and RPO ~0 (no accepted loss for cached context) — agreed on sequence-level strategy to replicate minimal KV state for in-flight sessions.
- Model variant fallback: primary is fp16 LlamaX/Redwood-opt tuned. On saturation should fallback to int8 quantized variant (reduced throughput per-token cost) then to a smaller family (e.g., Redwood-3-small) with degraded quality. Need rules: only fallback when latency SLO at p95 breaches for >2 minutes and after autoscaling attempts. Must expose fallback events via audit logs + webhook to their ops.
- Graceful degradation mechanics: prioritize leaderboards (high-value users) to full-quality model; low-priority users get cached/quantized path. Customer wants routing policy by customer tier + region + cost/p95 thresholds.
- Batching & cache policy: suggested prefix caching for common telemetry prompts; suggested KV eviction TTL 15m for active sessions to preserve chat continuity during failover.

POC & test plan: 2-week POC; Day 1-3: warm-up and baseline profiling; Day 4-9: sustained 80% load soak with incremental spikes to 120%; Day 10: simulate region outage and validate cross-region failover (measuring RTO/RPO and p95 change); Day 11-14: run model saturation test forcing fallback chain and evaluate quality/regression against eval set (linked). Results to be measured with latency, cost per token, and regressions on NLG quality metrics.

Open items / Ask from Redwood:
1) Fill reserved GPU worksheet (by Redwood) with pricing for 8x/12x/16x capacity and burst allowances.
2) Draft SLA addendum including p95 latency SLO and failover credits.
3) Provide detailed plan for KV replication or pre-warm strategy for cross-region standby.
4) Confirm audit log webhook payload for fallback events and frequency.

Recent quotes / paraphrases: "We need predictable tail latency — we can't have chat timeouts in customer support flows"; "Procurement will not accept open ended egress exposure".

Next step: AE to deliver filled capacity worksheet + draft SLA by 2026-03-22, schedule technical kick-off for POC (SE + infra) week of 2026-03-29.
